questions.prompt: A share's close goes from 40 to 45. What is the return?
questions.explanation: The return is (45 − 40) / 40 = 0.125, a gain of 12.5%. You divide the change by the starting price, 40.

questions.prompt: The same share then falls from 45 back to 40. Why is this loss smaller in percent than the 12.5% gain before it?
options: Because losses are always rounded down
Because the fall is measured from 45, a bigger starting price, so the same 5 pounds is a smaller fraction
Because the fall was 5 pounds and the rise was more
Because a return cannot be negative
questions.explanation: The return is (40 − 45) / 45 = −0.111, a loss of 11.1%. The same 5 pounds is divided by 45 instead of 40, so it is a smaller fraction.

questions.prompt: Share A rises from 50 to 55, and share B rises from 200 to 205. Which statement is right?
options: Both did equally well, because both rose by 5 pounds
B did better, because its price is higher
You cannot compare them, because their prices differ
A did better: its return is 10% and B's is 2.5%
questions.explanation: Returns divide the change by the starting price, so they compare shares at any price. A gained (55 − 50) / 50 = 10% and B gained (205 − 200) / 200 = 2.5%.
